papers.title: Detecting and Preventing Data Poisoning Attacks on AI Models
papers.abstract: This paper investigates the critical issue of data poisoning attacks on AI models, a growing concern in the ever-evolving landscape of artificial intelligence and cybersecurity. As advanced technology systems become increasingly prevalent across various sectors, the need for robust defence mechanisms against adversarial attacks becomes paramount. The study aims to develop and evaluate novel techniques for detecting and preventing data poisoning attacks, focusing on both theoretical frameworks and practical applications. Through a comprehensive literature review, experimental validation using the CIFAR-10 and Insurance Claims datasets, and the development of innovative algorithms, this paper seeks to enhance the resilience of AI models against malicious data manipulation. The study explores various methods, including anomaly detection, robust optimization strategies, and ensemble learning, to identify and mitigate the effects of poisoned data during model training. Experimental results indicate that data poisoning significantly degrades model performance, reducing classification accuracy by up to 27 % in image recognition tasks (CIFAR-10) and 22 % in fraud detection models (Insurance Claims dataset). The proposed defence mechanisms, including statistical anomaly detection and adversarial training, successfully mitigated poisoning effects, improving model robustness and restoring accuracy levels by an average of $15-20 \%$. The findings further demonstrate that ensemble learning techniques provide an additional layer of resilience, reducing false positives and false negatives caused by adversarial data injections. The findings of this paper contribute to the broader understanding of adversarial machine learning and provide actionable insights for practitioners in industries facing emerging threats to AI-based systems. By addressing the challenges of data poisoning attacks, this study aims to improve the security and reliability of AI models, ultimately fostering greater trust in AI technologies across critical applications.

papers.title: Robust and Adaptive Dual-Defense Framework Against Data Poisoning Attacks in Recommendation Systems
papers.abstract: Deep learning-based recommendation systems are highly vulnerable to data poisoning attacks, where adversaries manipulate user interactions to degrade model integrity. We hypothesize that combining an active robust loss with a passive GAN-based detection will significantly reduce poisoning impact in recommendation systems without sacrificing utility. We propose a robust and adaptive dual-defense framework: the active defense integrates a crafted loss function to mitigate poisoning effects while maintaining model performance. The passive defense employs a Generative Adversarial Network (GAN)-based detection model to identify and filter poisoned data, enhancing detection accuracy and system security. The framework supports classical matrix factorization (MF) model and large language model (LLM)-based pipelines and scales to large datasets. Extensive experiments across multiple real-world datasets at varying poison rates show that our method outperforms representative defenses, consistently reducing attack success without sacrificing recommendation quality. The framework also admits a federated instantiation, where robust training and GAN-based detection run on clients and only privacy-preserving summaries are aggregated. The proposed method significantly improves the robustness and adaptability of recommendation systems under data poisoning attacks.

papers.title: Adaptive AI-Driven Learning Architecture for Real Time Detection and Prevention of Data Poisoning and Model Evasion Attacks
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) has been integrated into cybersecurity systems particularly in cyber threat intelligence (CTI) and has significantly enhanced the detection, analysis, and mitigation of sophisticated cyber threats in real time in organisations. Unlike traditional static defence mechanisms, which rely on fixed rules or offline retraining, the proposed architecture empowers continuous dynamic learning capabilities to identify and mitigate attacks as they unfold ensuring the integrity and reliability of AI-driven CTI systems. AI models to self-heal and harden against evolving adversarial tactics. The primary goal is to enhance CTI operations by providing timely, accurate threat detection and robust mitigation thereby reducing the window of opportunity for attackers and improving overall cybersecurity posture. This article presents a comprehensive adaptive learning architecture with formalised threat models, architectural specifications, and empirical validation. Experimental evaluation using benchmark datasets (CIC-IDS2017 and VirusTotal) demonstrates that the system achieves 43.7% higher evasion detection accuracy than traditional static anomaly detectors, while maintaining processing latency below 5 milliseconds. The architecture successfully detects 89.1% of poisoning attacks and reduces false positive rates by 37.5% relative to baseline methods. The key contributions of this article include the design of an integrated adaptive learning system that simultaneously detects and prevents both data poisoning and model evasion attacks within cybersecurity AI models.

papers.title: Resilient Autonomy: Securing Intelligent Systems Against Adversarial Attacks
papers.abstract: As autonomous systems become central to mission-critical operations, their ability to withstand adversarial threats is crucial to ensuring trust, safety, and uninterrupted functionality. This paper introduces a comprehensive framework for resilient autonomy that proactively prevents, detects, and mitigates key adversarial challenges, including sensor spoofing, sensor manipulation, and machine learning model poisoning. We present a layered defense architecture that integrates adversarial robust learning, real-time anomaly detection, and secure control strategies to maintain reliable autonomous behavior in compromised environments. Our hybrid resilience model addresses both inference-time perturbations and upstream vulnerabilities in data acquisition and processing pipelines. The system employs adaptive decision logic and decentralized failover mechanisms to dynamically reconfigure operations upon detection of anomalies or suspicious behavior, thus preserving mission continuity. In addition, we embed explainable AI modules to enhance transparency, facilitate system diagnostics, and support operator trust. We validate the proposed framework using a suite of simulated adversarial scenarios across diverse autonomous agents, including drones, mobile robots, and vehicle models. Results demonstrate significant gains in threat resistance, operational stability, and recovery time when compared to conventional defenses. This work lays the foundation for building self-reliant, attack-aware autonomous systems that are capable of sustaining functionality under adversarial uncertainty.

papers.title: MedRAGShield: A Three-Tier Defense Framework Against Document Poisoning and Adversarial Attacks in Medical Retrieval-Augmented Generation Systems
papers.abstract: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems deployed in medical question-answering applications introduce novel attack surfaces not addressed by existing large language model (LLM) safety mechanisms. We present MedRAGShield, a three-tier middleware defense framework designed to detect and neutralise document injection poisoning, hallucination exploitation, prompt injection, and jailbreak attacks against medical RAG pipelines. Our system operates across three independently togglable defense modes: a baseline mode with no filtering, a confidence and hallucination gating mode, and a full defense mode augmenting the prior modes with Domain-Aware Sanity Check (DASC) rules that apply medical ontological constraints to generated outputs. We construct a 40-query adversarial evaluation dataset spanning four attack categories and conduct empirical evaluation on a clinical pharmacology RAG system built on Llama 3.2:3B and ChromaDB. Results demonstrate that confidence-based defenses alone are insufficient against highsimilarity document poisoning attacks, which achieve retrieval confidence exceeding 0.85 while delivering clinically dangerous misinformation a phenomenon we term the high-confidence poisoning paradox. The full MedRAGShield defense reduces Attack Success Rate (ASR) from 13.2% (undefended) to 0.0%, with block rate increasing from 0% to 62.5%, while maintaining sub-second query latency. This work establishes a reproducible evaluation methodology for medical RAG security and identifies domain-specific semantic rule checking as a critical missing layer in current LLM defense architectures. Code, dataset, and defense rules are openly available.

literature_themes.theme: Data Poisoning Attacks and Defense Mechanisms in AI Models
literature_themes.summary: This cluster of papers primarily investigates the vulnerabilities of AI models, particularly in the context of data poisoning attacks, and proposes various defense mechanisms. The studies explore adaptive learning architectures, dual-defense frameworks, and robust training techniques to enhance the resilience of AI systems against adversarial attacks. Experimental results demonstrate significant improvements in detection accuracy and model performance across different applications, including recommendation systems and cybersecurity.
literature_themes.limitations: Several papers lack comprehensive abstracts, limiting the understanding of their methodologies and findings. Additionally, while various defense mechanisms are proposed, the effectiveness of these approaches in real-world scenarios and against evolving attack strategies remains underexplored. The need for standardized evaluation metrics and benchmarks is also evident.
literature_themes.gap_relevance: This cluster highlights the critical need for ongoing research into adaptive defenses against data poisoning, particularly in dynamic environments. It underscores the importance of developing robust AI systems that can self-heal and adapt to new threats, thus identifying a significant research gap in the integration of continuous learning and real-time threat mitigation.

literature_themes.summary: This cluster focuses on enhancing the resilience of autonomous systems against adversarial attacks. It introduces a layered defense architecture that combines adversarial robust learning, real-time anomaly detection, and secure control strategies to ensure reliable operation in compromised environments. The framework emphasizes proactive prevention, detection, and mitigation of threats such as sensor spoofing and model poisoning, while incorporating explainable AI to improve transparency and operator trust.
literature_themes.limitations: The proposed framework may face challenges in real-world implementation, such as the complexity of integrating multiple defense layers and the potential for unforeseen adversarial tactics. Additionally, the reliance on simulations may not fully capture the dynamic nature of actual operational environments.
literature_themes.gap_relevance: This cluster highlights the need for further research into the practical application of resilient autonomy frameworks, particularly in diverse and unpredictable settings. It identifies gaps in understanding the long-term effectiveness of these defenses and the need for continuous adaptation to emerging threats.

literature_themes.theme: Defense Mechanisms in Medical Retrieval-Augmented Generation Systems
literature_themes.summary: This cluster focuses on the vulnerabilities of Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems in medical applications, particularly concerning document poisoning and adversarial attacks. It introduces MedRAGShield, a three-tier defense framework that includes various modes to detect and neutralize different types of attacks, demonstrating that traditional confidence-based defenses are inadequate against sophisticated threats.
literature_themes.limitations: The proposed defense mechanisms may not cover all potential attack vectors, and the empirical evaluation is limited to a specific clinical pharmacology RAG system, which may not generalize across all medical domains. Additionally, the effectiveness of the Domain-Aware Sanity Check (DASC) rules needs further validation.
literature_themes.gap_relevance: This cluster highlights the critical need for enhanced safety mechanisms in medical AI systems, identifying gaps in current defenses against adversarial attacks, thus supporting future research aimed at developing more robust solutions.

summary: The literature on robust AI systems against data poisoning and adversarial attacks reveals significant vulnerabilities and proposes various defense mechanisms, including adaptive learning architectures and layered defense frameworks. Key contributions include the development of MedRAGShield for medical applications and dual-defense strategies for recommendation systems, though limitations in generalizability and real-world applicability persist. A critical research gap remains in the need for standardized evaluation metrics and the exploration of adaptive defenses in dynamic environments.
scholarly_positioning: Despite significant advancements in defense mechanisms against data poisoning and adversarial attacks, existing frameworks often lack generalizability and real-world applicability, particularly in dynamic environments. Prior approaches, such as MedRAGShield and dual-defense strategies, demonstrate promise but are limited to specific domains and fail to address the evolving nature of threats comprehensively. This research proposes a novel adaptive learning architecture that not only enhances real-time detection and mitigation but also emphasizes the integration of standardized evaluation metrics to ensure broader applicability. By addressing these unresolved tensions, the proposed work situates itself within the critical discourse on resilient AI systems, aiming to bridge the gap between theoretical advancements and practical implementations.
domain_router: machine-learning method development; The appropriate methodology template includes adaptive learning architectures, real-time detection and mitigation techniques, and standardized evaluation metrics for performance assessment.
research_scope: This study will focus on developing an adaptive learning architecture for enhancing the resilience of recommendation systems against data poisoning attacks. The target population will consist of users interacting with these systems in e-commerce settings. The AI intervention will involve implementing a dual-defense framework that combines active robust loss and GAN-based detection over a six-month evaluation period. The comparison group will consist of traditional recommendation systems without the proposed defenses. Primary outcomes will include the reduction in attack success rates and improvements in recommendation accuracy, while secondary outcomes will assess user satisfaction and trust in the system. This research aims to provide empirical evidence on the effectiveness of adaptive defenses in real-world applications.
concept_definition: 1. Adaptive Learning Architecture: A machine learning framework that adjusts its learning process in real-time based on incoming data and evolving attack strategies to enhance system resilience. 2. Data Poisoning Attacks: Malicious attempts to manipulate the training data of a machine learning model, aiming to degrade its performance or mislead its predictions. 3. Dual-Defense Framework: A combined approach utilizing two distinct defensive strategies, specifically active robust loss and GAN-based detection, to mitigate the impact of data poisoning. 4. Active Robust Loss: A loss function designed to minimize the influence of poisoned data during model training, enhancing robustness against adversarial inputs. 5. GAN-based Detection: A technique employing Generative Adversarial Networks to identify and filter out malicious data points in real-time. 6. Recommendation Systems: Algorithms that suggest products or services to users based on their preferences and behavior, particularly in e-commerce settings. 7. Attack Success Rates: The frequency at which data poisoning attempts successfully degrade the performance of the recommendation system. 8. Recommendation Accuracy: The degree to which the recommendations made by the system align with user preferences and needs. 9. User Satisfaction: A measure of how well the system meets user expectations, often assessed through surveys or feedback mechanisms. 10. Trust in the System: The degree of confidence users have in the recommendation system, influenced by perceived transparency, reliability of recommendations, and system performance. 11. Real-time Detection and Mitigation Techniques: Methods that allow for the immediate identification and response to data poisoning attempts as they occur, ensuring ongoing system integrity. 12. Standardized Evaluation Metrics: Predefined criteria used to assess the effectiveness of the proposed defenses, including statistical measures for performance assessment.
technical_feasibility: The study requires access to labeled datasets for training and evaluation, as well as GPU resources for model training and real-time detection implementation. Since user satisfaction and trust are assessed, a human-subject design is necessary, which will require ethics approval. The design may also benefit from open-source model access for transparency and adaptability verification. If only API models are available, the design should be adjusted to focus on output-level evaluation rather than internal mechanisms. Missing resources include a clear plan for ethics approval and participant recruitment. A feasible adjustment is to include a detailed protocol for obtaining ethics approval and participant consent.
gap: Prior studies have demonstrated the effectiveness of dual-defense frameworks against data poisoning attacks in recommendation systems; however, they treat the adaptability of these defenses to evolving attack strategies as unresolved, leaving unclear whether real-time adaptive learning can significantly enhance resilience in dynamic environments. This matters practically because the rapid evolution of attack techniques necessitates systems that can continuously adapt to maintain effectiveness; therefore, this study investigates the integration of adaptive learning architectures to improve the resilience of recommendation systems against data poisoning attacks in e-commerce settings.
question: How does the implementation of an adaptive learning architecture, utilizing a dual-defense framework, impact the attack success rates and recommendation accuracy of e-commerce recommendation systems compared to traditional systems without these defenses?
theoretical_mechanism: The independent variable is the implementation of an adaptive learning architecture utilizing a dual-defense framework. The mediator is the real-time detection and mitigation techniques that enhance the system's resilience against data poisoning attacks. The dependent variables are the attack success rates and recommendation accuracy of e-commerce recommendation systems. The theoretical framework is grounded in adaptive learning principles, which suggest that systems can dynamically adjust to evolving threats. The causal chain posits that the integration of adaptive defenses leads to improved system-level outcomes (reduced attack success rates and increased recommendation accuracy) through enhanced technical mechanisms (real-time detection and robust loss functions). User-level outcomes, such as user satisfaction and trust, are influenced by perceived transparency and the reliability of recommendations, which must be empirically validated. Assumptions include that users will respond positively to improvements in system performance and that the adaptive mechanisms will effectively counteract evolving data poisoning strategies.
hypothesis: The implementation of an adaptive learning architecture utilizing a dual-defense framework will significantly reduce the attack success rates of e-commerce recommendation systems compared to traditional systems without these defenses, mediated by enhanced real-time detection and mitigation techniques.

methodology: This study will employ an adaptive learning architecture integrated with a dual-defense framework to enhance the resilience of e-commerce recommendation systems against data poisoning attacks. Participants will include users interacting with these systems, with a six-month evaluation period. The experimental group will utilize the dual-defense framework, while the control group will consist of traditional recommendation systems without these defenses. Operationalized variables include attack success rates and recommendation accuracy, measured through system logs and user interaction metrics. Evaluation metrics will focus on detection accuracy, user satisfaction, and trust, assessed via surveys post-interaction. Statistical reasoning will involve comparing means between groups using appropriate tests to validate the effectiveness of the adaptive defenses. Confound controls will account for user demographics and prior experience, ensuring reproducibility and scope control by limiting the study to specific e-commerce contexts.
phd_contribution_design: This research introduces an adaptive learning architecture that enhances the resilience of recommendation systems against evolving data poisoning attacks, framed within adaptive learning principles that emphasize dynamic system adjustments. The mechanism-level claim posits that real-time detection and mitigation techniques, integrated within a dual-defense framework, will significantly reduce attack success rates and improve recommendation accuracy. Existing literature fails to adequately address the adaptability of defenses in real-world, dynamic environments, leaving a gap in understanding how these systems can evolve alongside attack strategies. The falsifiable claim is that the implementation of this adaptive architecture will lead to a statistically significant reduction in attack success rates compared to traditional systems. The strongest baseline for comparison will be traditional recommendation systems without adaptive defenses. Evidence supporting this claim will be established through empirical results demonstrating improved detection accuracy and reduced attack success rates. A negative result would indicate that the proposed adaptive mechanisms do not provide a significant advantage, suggesting a need for reevaluation of the adaptability concept in AI resilience frameworks.
pre_proposal_critique: The proposed contribution design risks falling short of an 85+ PhD-level score due to several critical weaknesses. First, the novelty claim lacks sufficient differentiation from existing dual-defense frameworks, which may lead to a perception of incremental rather than transformative advancement. To address this, the proposal must explicitly articulate how the integration of active robust loss and GAN-based detection is fundamentally different and more effective than prior work. Second, the theoretical framework is underdeveloped, failing to robustly connect adaptive learning principles to the specific mechanisms of resilience in recommendation systems. This requires a more detailed theoretical justification that links adaptive learning to measurable outcomes in the context of evolving attack strategies. Lastly, the baseline comparison with traditional systems is weak; the proposal should include a comprehensive ablation study that isolates the effects of each component of the dual-defense framework to validate its effectiveness. By addressing these objections, the proposal can enhance its clarity, depth, and overall rigor.

proposal: This research proposes a novel adaptive learning architecture designed to enhance the resilience of e-commerce recommendation systems against data poisoning attacks, addressing critical gaps in existing literature that inadequately account for the adaptability of defenses in dynamic environments. Prior work, such as dual-defense frameworks, has shown promise but often lacks empirical validation in real-world settings and fails to integrate mechanisms that allow for continuous adaptation to evolving threats. This study will implement a dual-defense framework combining active robust loss and GAN-based detection, hypothesizing that this integration will significantly reduce attack success rates and improve recommendation accuracy compared to traditional systems. The methodology includes a six-month evaluation with users, employing robust controls for demographics and prior experience, and operationalizing constructs such as attack success rates (measured through system logs), recommendation accuracy (assessed via user interaction metrics), and user satisfaction (gathered from post-interaction surveys). A comprehensive risk management strategy will address potential ethical concerns, participant recruitment, and confounding variables, ensuring reproducibility and robustness in evaluation. By situating this research within the adaptive learning principles, the study aims to provide empirical evidence that demonstrates how real-time detection and mitigation techniques can enhance system resilience, thereby contributing to the theoretical understanding of AI defenses and offering practical guidelines for implementation in e-commerce environments.

proposal_critique.revision_plan: Revise the gap stage to clarify how the proposed research builds on existing work and addresses unresolved issues. Strengthen the scholarly positioning by providing a critical analysis of prior approaches. Ensure that the methodology is detailed, particularly in defining the user population and the specifics of the intervention and control groups.

rubric_scores.level: 9-11: understandable but partially broad or insufficiently operationalized
rubric_scores.justification: The proposal identifies a relevant research problem regarding the resilience of recommendation systems against data poisoning attacks. However, the operational definitions of key concepts such as 'adaptive learning architecture' and 'dual-defense framework' are not sufficiently detailed, leading to some ambiguity in the research boundaries. Major weaknesses: Key concepts are not fully operationalized, and the framing lacks specificity regarding the unique contributions of the proposed architecture compared to existing frameworks. Next band requirements: To move into the next band, the proposal must provide clearer operational definitions of the constructs and more precise boundaries of the research problem.

rubric_scores.level: 9-11: generally connected but some weak transitions or unsupported assumptions
rubric_scores.justification: The proposal presents a logical flow from the problem to the hypothesis and methodology. However, there are gaps in the justification of assumptions, particularly regarding the effectiveness of the proposed dual-defense framework. Major weaknesses: Some causal claims are not sufficiently supported by the literature, and the transitions between the theoretical framework and empirical testing are weak. Next band requirements: Strengthening the justification for causal claims and ensuring that all assumptions are backed by relevant literature would improve coherence.

The proposal introduces an adaptive learning architecture and a dual-defense framework, which are relevant contributions. However, the novelty is somewhat diminished by the reliance on existing concepts without a clear articulation of how they are uniquely combined or improved. Major weaknesses: The proposal does not sufficiently differentiate its contributions from existing dual-defense frameworks, leading to a perception of incremental advancement. Next band requirements: Explicitly articulating the unique aspects of the proposed framework and demonstrating how it advances the field would enhance the novelty score.

The methodology is generally sound, with a clear plan for evaluation and controls. However, the proposal lacks a detailed ablation study to isolate the effects of each component of the dual-defense framework. Major weaknesses: The absence of a comprehensive ablation study weakens the methodological rigor and the ability to draw strong conclusions from the results. Next band requirements: Including a detailed ablation study and a stronger justification for the chosen evaluation metrics would enhance the feasibility score.

rubric_scores.level: 9-11: relevant literature used but somewhat surface-level
rubric_scores.justification: The proposal engages with relevant literature but lacks depth in critical synthesis and comparative analysis. It identifies gaps but does not sufficiently articulate why existing work is inadequate. Major weaknesses: The literature review is somewhat superficial, lacking a nuanced understanding of competing approaches and unresolved tensions in the field. Next band requirements: A deeper engagement with the literature, including a critical synthesis of methodologies and identification of unresolved issues, would improve the score.

rubric_scores.level: 5-6: strong master-level but limited theoretical depth
rubric_scores.justification: While the proposal demonstrates some theoretical understanding, it lacks the depth necessary for PhD-level work, particularly in articulating the mechanisms underlying the proposed framework. Major weaknesses: The theoretical framework is underdeveloped, and there is insufficient discussion of limitations and trade-offs associated with the proposed methods. Next band requirements: Enhancing the theoretical depth by discussing the mechanisms in detail and addressing potential limitations would elevate the proposal to a PhD-level depth.

The proposal is generally well-structured and clear, but some sections could benefit from improved conciseness and precision. Major weaknesses: There are instances of repetitive phrasing and a lack of clarity in some definitions, which detracts from overall readability. Next band requirements: Improving clarity and conciseness in the writing would enhance the overall presentation score.

evaluation.comments: Total score: 67.0/100. Academic level: Master-level. Major strengths: Identifies a relevant research problem in AI resilience.; Proposes a dual-defense framework with potential practical applications. Major weaknesses: Insufficient operationalization of key concepts.; Weak justification for causal claims and assumptions.; Limited novelty and differentiation from existing frameworks. Required improvements for true PhD-level quality: Provide clearer operational definitions and research boundaries.; Strengthen the theoretical framework and causal reasoning.; Enhance the literature review with deeper critical synthesis. Final verdict: The proposal demonstrates some foundational research maturity but lacks the depth, rigor, and originality expected at the PhD level.
